geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing emphasis into a courtyard organization to establish a real public void and strengthen program fit.
Increase the void size so it reads as usable ground space rather than decorative subtraction.
Open the court toward the verified access side to repair the public threshold relation.

graph_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant mass into a courtyard-based composition so the building opens to a usable public void instead of reading as a sealed split bar.
Enlarge the court so the subtraction becomes occupiable and legible as neighborhood public space.
Align the public opening to the verified access side in the program frame.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early massing idea in plan and is not visually fragmented, but it is too small in void logic and too semantically sealed for the neighborhood-living brief. Across views, the dominant move is a compact split bar with a shallow notch and roof articulation; however, the open space figure is weak and does not become a clearly occupiable court, terrace, or active frontage response. The verified access edge is not answered by a strong public void or entry seam, so the ground relation remains underdeveloped. The form is repairable and internally consistent, but program fit fails because the section does not yet express a convincing active mixed-use ground with public threshold and upper hierarchy. The mass also skews generic and boxy rather than showing a distinctive neighborhood-building section.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Tower-like vertical emphasis is much stronger than this neighborhood-living brief; the candidate is more horizontal and low, so only the sectional sharpening principle transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Tapered/stepped upper mass can sharpen a dominant street-building gesture when paired with a clearer public base or threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower typology is not program-matched; the candidate should not borrow the vertical tower strategy.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A singular tall mass can read coherently if the base and crown are differentiated by a clear section logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is much smaller and more pavilion-like, so only the active-ground-edge logic transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple grounded base with a legible canopy/threshold toward the street can make the access edge read clearly.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate currently lacks the strong continuous sectional promenade and terraced public generosity seen here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/terrace and sectional continuity can support neighborhood living while preserving a public void and upper hierarchy.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the visible views, but the access-edge response is semantically weak.
The form is coherent in more than one view, so this is not a pure view-dependent false positive; the main failure is program and threshold logic.
The current split-wing language is not enough to count as a meaningful public void.
